QF.id: SIA Social Impact Assessment and Assessors_2

question.text: Ms. Sunita Patil, a newly empanelled SIA, is explaining to a client why the SEBI framework prefers the term 'Social Impact Assessment' over 'Social Audit'. Which statement is MOST accurate under SEBI ICDR Regulations?

answer.text: SEBI ICDR Regulations have replaced the term 'Social Audit' with 'Social Impact Assessment', though both share similar principles of evaluating social outcomes, stakeholder engagement, and transparency
Social Audit is now prohibited and Social Impact Assessment is a legally distinct regime with different principles
Social Audit is still used for CSR while Social Impact Assessment is only for the Social Stock Exchange ecosystem
The two terms continue in parallel in SEBI ICDR Regulations with no functional difference in underlying work

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 5.1.1 is explicit: 'As per SEBI Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR) Regulations, the term Social Audit has been replaced with the term Social Impact Assessment. However, SIA and Social Audit share similar principles and focus on assessing the social impacts of developmental projects.' So the terminology changed but the substance carried over. The Trap: Option B overstates — social audit was not prohibited, it was re-termed in the SEBI context. Option C wrongly suggests dual nomenclature running in parallel by regulatory carve-out — actually SEBI simply swapped the term. Option D wrongly says they run in parallel; in SEBI ICDR the term was replaced. Cross-Exam Context: NISM III-A / III-C (Compliance) and NISM XV (Research Analyst) also touch SSE-listed entity disclosure. XXIII uses SIA language throughout; candidates from prior exams must update vocabulary from 'social audit' to 'SIA' when engaging with SSE work. Assessor's Pro-Tip: On your engagement letter, always use the SEBI term 'Social Impact Assessment' even if the SE casually calls it a 'social audit'. Auditors who carry forward the old term in reports have seen their report title flagged during ICAI SIAB peer review.
